# STRATA: Descent — Game Design Specification

**Status:** design ready for implementation
**Engine:** three.js (r160+), ES modules, Vite
**Art pipeline:** every visual asset generated by the connected ComfyUI MCP server using the registered `z_image_turbo` workflow
**Document role:** this file is the single source of truth. It is written so it can be handed to an implementing agent or developer as-is and followed without further questions.

---

## 0. Kickoff prompt (copy-paste this to start implementation)

> Build **STRATA: Descent** exactly as specified in `GAME_DESIGN_SPEC.md` in this repo. Use three.js with ES modules under `src/`, data-driven tables under `data/`, and all art under `assets/images/`. Generate every image with the ComfyUI MCP tools: fetch the saved template `z_image_turbo` with `get_workflow_template`, patch only node `57:27` `.text`, node `57:13` `.width`/`.height`, node `57:3` `.seed`/`.steps`, and node `9` `.filename_prefix`, then submit with `generate_with_workflow`. Never use the default `generate_image` tool, never edit the saved template, and never change model loaders, CFG, sampler, scheduler, shift, or node connections. Download each result from the returned ComfyUI URL into `assets/images/<family>/` with the canonical filename from §13, and log every generation into `assets/images/manifest.json` (prompt, seed, steps, size, source URL, output path). Leave `assets/music/` empty and respect the music contract in §12.

---

## 1. Concept

A photorealistic first-person dungeon crawler. You descend an endless procedurally generated dungeon. Each level is a maze containing exactly one staircase down. Kill things, collect better gear by walking over it, find the stairs, go deeper, get stronger, die eventually, beat your run.

**Design pillars**

1. **One decision per moment** — every pickup is a yes/no you make by moving, every enemy is one readable threat.
2. **Depth is the progression system** — no XP menu, no crafting screen. Better depth = better gear = visibly stronger player.
3. **Photoreal but staged** — real materials, game framing. Everything reads like a studio-lit board game piece, not a photograph of a real place.
4. **Short, repeatable runs** — a run should die in 8–20 minutes. Runs must be replayable from a seed.

**Player fantasy:** an armed nobody falling further and further into a place that keeps outfitting you.

---

## 2. Experience targets

| Target | Value |
|---|---|
| Session length (one run) | 8–20 min |
| Time per level | 60–150 s |
| Typical death depth | 6–12 |
| Input | mouse + keyboard, pointer lock; gamepad stretch goal |
| Frame budget | 60 fps on a mid desktop GPU; ≥30 fps on integrated graphics |
| Draw calls / level | ≤ 120 (instanced geometry) |
| Texture memory | ≤ 180 MB at 1024², mipmapped |
| Load time (cold, all assets) | ≤ 6 s |
| Offline | yes, after first load |

---

## 3. Camera, movement, and level representation

**Decision: first-person, free movement, 2.5D entity rendering.**

- First-person camera at eye height 1.65 m, pointer-lock mouse look, pitch clamp ±85°.
- WASD movement, walk 3.2 m/s, Shift to jog 4.6 m/s, no jump, no crouch. Collision = cylinder radius 0.35 m against wall AABBs, sliding along walls.
- The world is a **grid of cells** (1 cell = 2.0 m, wall height 3.6 m). Walls/floors/ceilings are real three.js geometry with tileable generated textures. Everything else — enemies, pickups, props, VFX — is a **billboarded sprite** made from a generated image.
- Sprites billboard around Y only (upright), so a photoreal orc sprite always reads as a standing creature from any angle. Pickups billboard fully.
- Each sprite gets a generated soft **contact-shadow decal** on the floor, which is what makes 2.5D sprites sit in a 3D space convincingly.
- Player is never rendered. Sword/bow viewmodel: a generated weapon sprite pinned bottom-right, animated with a swing arc (see §7).

Why 2.5D and not 3D meshes: the asset generator produces images, not meshes. Photoreal sprites on a real 3D maze with real lighting, fog and shadows gives the "photoreal dungeon" look at a fraction of the risk and cost. A mesh pass is listed as a stretch goal in §18.

---

## 4. Core loop

1. Level starts: player at entry cell, level banner + depth number, random music track from `assets/music/`.
2. Explore the maze. Torches light the way; fog hides unexplored areas.
3. Fight or avoid enemies. Kills drop loot on the floor.
4. Walk over an item: if it is better than what is equipped, it auto-equips; otherwise it is absorbed for score. Health and life pickups always apply.
5. Find the staircase. Walk onto it and hold for 1.5 s → descend.
6. Descending: +score, gear partially repaired, difficulty steps up, new maze, new random music.
7. Lose all lives → Game Over: depth reached, kills, score, seed, best-run table, retry/restart.

**Death mid-run:** lose one life, respawn at the level entry cell with full health and armor, 2.5 s invulnerability (screen flash), level and its loot persist, the staircase stays where it was. Lives are run-scoped unless you find ghost drops (§8).

---

## 5. Player stats

| Stat | Start | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Health | 100 / 100 | flat, never grows; survivability comes from armor and positioning |
| Armor (durability) | 0 / 0 | from equipped armor only |
| Lives | 3 | cap 5 |
| Weapon | Worn Short Sword | see §8 |
| Armor | none | |
| Score | 0 | kills + loot + depth |
| Depth | 1 | increments on descent |

**Damage resolution**

```
mitigation  = min(0.55, armor.tier * 0.09)          // 0 if no armor
raw         = incoming * (1 - mitigation)
if armor.durability > 0:
    toArmor = raw * 0.65
    toHp    = raw * 0.35
    armor.durability -= toArmor
    if armor.durability <= 0: armor breaks (broken overlay on armor bar, mitigation = 0)
else:
    toHp = raw
health -= toHp
```

**Repair:** on descent, armor regains 35 % of its max durability. A generated **Repair Kit** pickup (from brutes/mages, 12 % chance) restores 40 %. This keeps the armor bar a live resource without a shop.

**Health regen:** none outside pickups. Slimes are the main healing source, so healing is something you hunt for.

---

## 6. Enemies

Base roster of 6 families. Higher tiers are **reskins**: same behaviour, different generated sprite (and a slight tint/rim light), higher stats. Reskinning keeps the asset count sane and makes "that is the same thing but meaner" instantly readable.

### 6.1 Family definitions

| Family | HP | Damage | Speed | Behaviour | Signature tell |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Slime | 18 | 7 | 1.1 m/s | slow homing contact damage; 30 % chance splits into 2 Lesser Slimes on death | jiggles, squelch sound before lunge |
| Orc | 42 | 12 | 2.2 m/s | chase, close to 1.6 m, 0.6 s windup, 110° melee arc | raises weapon, grunt SFX |
| Archer | 30 | 14 (arrow) | 2.0 m/s | keeps 6–9 m, strafes, 0.9 s draw tell, fires linear projectile; flees if cornered | draw sound + laser-thin glint line for 0.3 s |
| Mage | 26 | 18 (fireball) | 1.6 m/s | casts slow homing fireball with 1.2 s cast; blinks 6 m away if player within 3.5 m | rising hum + glowing hands |
| Ghost | 34 | 10 | 2.6 m/s | drifts directly at player, **ignores armour**, passes through at most one wall per 4 s, idle-phases through walls otherwise | audio dropout + reverb voice |
| Spider (optional flavour) | 12 | 6 | 3.4 m/s | fast dart-and-retreat; web = 1.5 s slow | skitter SFX |

### 6.2 Tiers and reskins

| Family | Tier 1 (depth 1–3) | Tier 2 (4–6) | Tier 3 (7–9) | Tier 4 (10+) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Slime | Slime | Acid Slime | Caustic Ooze | Void Slime |
| Orc | Orc Grunt | Orc Brute | Orc Warlord | Iron Reaver |
| Archer | Goblin Archer | Bone Archer | Venom Archer | Hollow Ranger |
| Mage | Hedge Mage | Storm Mage | Void Archmage | Doomspeaker |
| Ghost | Wisp | Wraith | Dread Spectre | Hungering Shade |
| Spider | Cellar Spider | Grave Spider | Bone Spider | (none) |

Reskins carry their threat read in two places. The sprite changes bulk and damage — and,
for the ghost family, stance: a wisp has no planted feet and no free hands, a shade is a
full biped with claws. The renderer adds the rest with `heightByTier` per family in
`data/enemies.json`, so a tier-1 wisp is drawn 1.08 m and a tier-4 shade 2.16 m. Collision
radius is deliberately *not* ramped, so the ramp is presentation only and balance is
untouched. The integration suite asserts that each family's tier-1 height is below its
tier-4 height and that the tallest silhouette still clears a hallway ceiling.

Tier stat scaling:

```
tier        = 1 + floor((depth - 1) / 3)
hpMult      = 1 + 0.18 * (depth - 1)
dmgMult     = 1 + 0.15 * (depth - 1)
speedMult   = min(1.35, 1 + 0.04 * (depth - 1))
hp          = round(base.hp * hpMult * tier.hpMult)     // tier.hpMult = 1 / 1.6 / 2.4 / 3.4
damage      = round(base.damage * dmgMult * tier.dmgMult) // 1 / 1.5 / 2.1 / 2.8
```

**Miniboss every 3rd depth** (3, 6, 9, …): one elite, 4× HP, uses the same family move set plus a 360° burst attack, guaranteed drop at quality tier +2. Announced with a depth banner: "Something large is awake."

**Spawn rules**

```
count    = min(34, 7 + round(1.6 * depth))
mix      = depth-weighted (early: slime/orc heavy; archers from depth 2; mages from depth 3; ghosts from depth 4)
placement= BFS distance 8–40 cells from entry, ≥ 4 cells apart, never in the entry cell's room
stair guard = 0–2 enemies within 3 cells of the staircase (never on it)
```

---

## 7. Combat

**Player attack (melee — swords):** left click. Swing 0.45 s, cooldown 0.70 s, arc 110°, range 1.9 m (2.4 m for greatsword family). Hit = any sprite whose angle to camera is inside the arc and within range; single target per swing (no cleave until Masterwork tier adds `cleave: 2`). Damage = weapon damage × quality multiplier, ±10 % jitter, 12 % crit for ×1.75.

**Two weapon slots.** The player carries a melee weapon and a bow in separate slots, and `1` / `2` put one of them in hand. Equipping never transfers between slots: a bow picked up over a sword fills the empty ranged slot, so the loop stays "walk over it and get stronger" without the bow ever stealing the blade. The active weapon drives the viewmodel, the HUD highlight and the attack rule.

**Ammunition (revised — supersedes the original "infinite ammo" decision).** The bow is powerful, so it is rationed: one arrow per shot, archers always drop 1–3 arrows on death, and an empty quiver closes the ranged slot — `2` is refused with a reason, and firing the last arrow hands the melee weapon back immediately. The ranged slot is therefore gated on ammunition, not on owning a bow.

**Player attack (ranged — bows):** left click with a bow in hand and an arrow to spend. Draw 0.35 s, cooldown 0.90 s, arrow travels 24 m/s up to 18 m, damage falls off to 70 % at max range, 15 % crit.

**Projectiles are physical, visible objects.** Every arrow — the player's and an archer's — is a real moving sprite, not a hit-scan, and it must be aimed from the shooter toward its target. A projectile's direction may never default to the viewer's own facing: an archer behind you would then shoot away from you, which is exactly what an early build did. Both sides' arrows use the `items/arrow` sprite, fly point-first, and are oriented by a stated convention: an arrow crossing the view lies along its path, one receding shows its fletching, one closing shows its head. Sprite roll is applied inside the upright billboard, so the billboard pass has to reset orientation before rolling, or the roll compounds every frame.

**Enemy attack tells:** every enemy attack has a visible tell (0.3–1.2 s) and a distinct audio cue before damage lands. No enemy may deal damage without a tell. This is the main fairness mechanism.

**Feedback per hit:** damage number, hit spark sprite, enemy sprite flashes white 120 ms, light knockback 0.25 m, SFX pitch varies ±8 % so repeats do not grate.

**Player hurt feedback:** red vignette pulse, screen shake 0.15 (scaled by damage), directional arc indicating hit source.

## 8. Loot, quality, and auto-upgrade

### 8.1 Drop table

| Source | Drop | Chance | Slot |
|---|---|---|---|
| Orc family | Sword family | 55 % | weapon |
| Archer family | Bow family | 50 % | weapon (ranged slot) |
| Archer family | **Arrows ×1–3** | 100 % | ammo |
| Mage family | Armor family | 45 % | armor |
| Slime family | Health Draught | 90 % | instant (heal 25–45) |
| Ghost family | Extra Life | 35 % | instant (+1 life, cap 5) |
| Spider family | Coin | 60 % | score |
| Any enemy | Coin | 25 % | score (1–3 × tier) |
| Brute / Mage / miniboss | Repair Kit | 12 % | instant (+40 % armour durability) |
| Miniboss | guaranteed gear, quality tier +2 | 100 % | weapon or armor |

Drops land as physical sprites where the enemy died, bob gently, and glow faintly with their rarity colour. They persist for the whole level. Treasure pedestals in dead ends are the exception to the ammunition rule: a pedestal that holds a bow also holds **5 arrows** beside it, so a bow found before any archer is met is a working weapon on pickup rather than a promise.

### 8.2 Weapon and armor families

| Weapons | base dmg | notes |
|---|---|---|
| Short Sword | 14 | fast, 1.9 m |
| Longsword | 18 | |
| Battle Axe | 26 | slower, cooldown 0.95 s, arc 130° |
| Greatsword | 32 | cooldown 1.15 s, `cleave: 2` |
| Hunting Bow | 12 | ranged 18 m |
| War Bow | 17 | ranged 22 m |
| Longbow | 23 | ranged 26 m, slower draw |

| Armor | max durability | tier (mitigation) |
|---|---|---|
| Padded Jack | 40 | 1 |
| Studded Leather | 70 | 2 |
| Chainmail | 105 | 3 |
| Plated Cuirass | 150 | 4 |
| Warded Plate | 210 | 5 (best available) |

### 8.3 Quality system (the "not always the same" requirement)

```
baseTier = weighted(depth) + bossBonus          // 0..5
jitter   = 0.88 + random() * 0.24               // ±12 % continuous
quality  = tiers[baseTier].mult * jitter
score    = round(base.stat * quality)
```

| Tier | Name | Mult | Prefix example | Colour (UI glow, hex) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Worn | 0.75 | Worn Short Sword | `#9aa0a6` |
| 1 | Standard | 1.00 | Short Sword | `#e6e8ea` |
| 2 | Fine | 1.25 | Fine Longsword | `#5fb3f6` |
| 3 | Refined | 1.50 | Refined Battle Axe | `#4fd18b` |
| 4 | Masterwork | 1.85 | Masterwork Greatsword | `#c084fc` |
| 5 | Relic | 2.25 | Relic of the Deep | `#f5a524` |

Tier weights by depth (index = depth band):

```
depth 1-2 : [30, 45, 20, 5, 0, 0]
depth 3-5 : [10, 35, 35, 18, 2, 0]
depth 6-9 : [3, 15, 35, 35, 11, 1]
depth 10+ : [0, 5, 20, 35, 30, 10]
```

Rolls are independent per drop, so two orcs on the same level can drop swords 40 % apart in power.

**Endless depths (implementation note).** Shifting the weights past depth 10 was
simulated and it breaks the fantasy: by depth 14 every drop was Relic, which reads as
"loot stopped mattering". Past depth 10 the weights therefore stay at the `10+` row and
depth keeps scaling the *numbers* instead — an extra `+6 %` per depth on the resulting
stat (`endless = 1 + 0.06 × (depth − 10)` in `src/loot/quality.js`). `npm run test:loot`
asserts the mean rises across bands (47.5 → 55.3 → 63.9 → 75.8 → 84.7), the spread
stays wide (coefficient of variation 73–87 %), and two swords on one level differ by up
to 4× in score.

### 8.4 Auto-upgrade on contact

```
onTouch(item):
  if item.slot == 'weapon' or 'armor':
      if item.score > equipped.score:
          equipped = item; toast("EQUIPPED  <name>  (+Δ)"); sfx_equip
      else:
          score += item.score; toast("salvaged +<score>"); sfx_coin
  else: apply instantly
```

- The player never opens an inventory. Comparison is done for them; the toast plus a small "+Δ" is the only UI needed.
- Settings toggle `compareMode` (default off). When on, touching a *better* item shows a comparison card for 3 s and you must press E to accept — for players who want to keep a fast sword over a slow axe. Auto-upgrade stays the default because the request asks for it and it keeps the loop frictionless.
- A weapon swap changes the viewmodel sprite, swing SFX, and attack timing immediately.
- Salvaging weaker items is the score sink and makes stomping through a pile of junk feel productive rather than wasteful.

## 9. Level generation

### 9.1 Guarantee contract

Every generated level **must** satisfy, before it is accepted:

1. Staircase reachable from the entry cell (BFS over walkable cells).
2. Shortest entry→stairs path length ≥ 0.55 × maze diameter, so the level is a maze and not a hallway you walk down.
3. Every enemy and every pickup is on a reachable cell.
4. Entry cell and staircase cell are never the same and never adjacent (min Chebyshev distance 6).
5. No cell is enclosed by walls on all four sides.

Failure → regenerate. Up to 8 attempts, then fall back to a pure recursive-backtracker perfect maze, which satisfies 1–5 by construction. Never ship a level that fails validation; never silently skip the checks.

### 9.2 Generator

```
W = H = 25 (depth 1-3) → 33 (4-6) → 41 (7+)          // odd numbers, cell = 2.0 m
1. Carve a perfect maze with recursive backtracker on the odd grid.
2. Braid: open 15% (+5% per 3 depths, cap 35%) of dead ends to create loops.
   Loop-free mazes feel claustrophobic and make ghost/line-of-sight enemies unfair.
3. Carve 3–7 rooms, 5×5 to 9×9, never overlapping, each opening on ≥2 corridors.
4. Entry: a random cell in the corner quadrant with the fewest neighbours.
5. BFS from entry across all walkable cells → pick the farthest cell as the staircase.
6. Props: pillars in rooms, crates, rubble, cobwebs, 8–16 torch sconces (max 6 in the
   active light set; the rest are emissive-only).
7. Place loot alcoves: 2–4 dead-end cells get a guaranteed drop pedestal.
8. Place enemies and pickups per §6 spawn rules.
9. Validate §9.1. Assign tileset variant (§11) and seed.
```

Level seed is `runSeed + depth`, so a run is fully reproducible and "share seed" reproduces an entire descent.

### 9.3 Staircase interaction

Staircase is a generated sprite set into a floor opening, lit from below. Standing on it starts a 1.5 s hold ring around the crosshair. Moving off cancels. Completion: fade to black 0.4 s, depth banner, new maze, music crossfade, +`depth × 100` score, 35 % armour repair.

### 9.4 Ambience

Exponential fog, dark base (near plane 2 m, far plane 34 m, colour per biome §11). Torch point lights flicker with low-frequency noise. Player carries a faint warm headlamp cone so unlit corridors stay readable but dim. Occasional distant SFX (drip, skitter, stone settle) every 6–20 s from a random bearing.

---

## 10. HUD / UI

Persistent HUD (generated sprite frames, HTML/CSS text on top):

- **Health bar** bottom-left, `#e0483d` fill over dark glass, 320 px wide, pulses red under 30 %, numeric value inside.
- **Armor bar** directly under health, `#5b8fd6` fill, segmented ticks, "BROKEN" label with red hatching at 0 durability. Empty state (no armor) renders as a dimmed disabled bar with a shield-slash icon, not a hidden bar — the player should always see the slot they could fill.
- **Lives** as skull icons bottom-left of the bars (max 5; overflow shows "×6").
- **Depth + score** top-centre small; **weapon/armor icons** bottom-right with name and score, and a brief green flash on upgrade.
- **Crosshair** centre, generated, expands 4 px while drawing a bow.
- **Minimap** top-right, 180 px, canvas-drawn from the grid: explored cells only, unexplored = black, staircase shows once seen or revealed by a `Stair Sense` (unlocked depth 5+; pulses the stairs direction). Enemies shown only when visible.
- **Toasts** bottom-centre, max 3 stacked, 2.5 s.
- **Menus:** main menu (New Run / Seed / Settings / How to Play), pause (Esc), settings (mouse sensitivity, FOV 75–100, volume splits, compare mode, shader quality Low/Med/High), game over (depth, kills, score, best 5 runs in `localStorage`, Retry / New Run).
- **Level start banner:** "DEPTH 7" + biome name, 2 s, with the music track name in tiny type — so the player learns which track goes with which depth.

## 11. Art direction

**Photoreal, but staged.** Real-world materials — chisel marks, worn bronze, wet stone, scratched leather, subsurface on skin — always presented like a studio-lit game piece: centred subject, clean rim light, flat neutral backdrop, no scene clutter. This keeps generated sprites readable as sprites instead of pretending to be geometry.

**Look anchors**

- Palette per biome (rotates every 3 depths, from level seed):
  - Crypt (1–3): cold grey limestone + pale blue torchless light
  - Foundry (4–6): iron black + ember orange
  - Cavern (7–9): wet basalt + green phosphor
  - Vault (10+): obsidian + antique gold and violet
- Lighting: warm flickering point lights, hard shadow bias, no ambient above 0.12. Deep blacks are wanted; readability is handled by the player headlamp cone and emissive rim on interactables.
- Sprites: photoreal subject, alpha-keyed, plus a pre-generated contact-shadow decal. Slight in-engine chromatic aberration and vignette at screen edges sells "camera footage", not "render".
- Text is always real DOM/CSS type, never baked into generated images (image models produce unreliable text). Every prompt ends with `no text, no watermark, no lettering`.
- Item rarity is conveyed by an emitted glow colour + a generated ornate UI frame per rarity tier, never by re-generating 6 copies of each weapon.

**Sprite-key pipeline (critical technical note)**

Z-Image Turbo is text-to-image with no alpha channel, so every entity sprite must be generated on a flat chroma backdrop and keyed at load time:

- Background keyword in prompts: `isolated on flat solid magenta (#ff00ff) background, no floor, no cast shadow, no reflection`.
- `src/render/chromaKey.js` loads each sprite into a canvas, keys magenta (chroma distance threshold ~0.22, edge feather 1 px, despill on near-magenta pixels), caches the resulting RGBA texture. Runtime keying, no build dependencies, runs once per asset at load.
- **Tile seams are solved structurally, not by prompting.** The 50 %-offset review
  (`/seamcheck.html`, screenshot it headlessly) showed that Z-Image "seamless tileable"
  outputs carry a lighting gradient, so every raw tile shows a visible seam at its
  boundary. The engine therefore builds a **2x2 mirrored composite** of each tile
  (`src/render/assets.js getMirroredTexture`) and tiles that: wrap boundaries always
  meet a mirrored copy of the same edge pixels, so no seam is possible. Cost is a
  symmetric pattern that is faintly visible at very close range and invisible at
  gameplay distance under torch light. Regenerating with new seeds was tried first and
  did not fix it; do not treat "regenerate the tile" as the seam remedy.
- Sprites are keyed against a **sampled** backdrop colour, not an assumed `#ff00ff`:
  the border of the image is measured and keyed against that (the model never emits an
  exact colour). Measured against the generated set, this keyed cleanly with no magenta
  fringe on creature sprites.
- UI frames and bars must be generated with `symmetrical composition, flat even lighting, dark background` so they can be 9-sliced.

---

## 12. Audio

### 12.1 Music

The user supplies music files later. Code must work with the folder empty.

- Location: `assets/music/`
- Contract: `assets/music/manifest.json` → `{ "tracks": ["track01.mp3", ...] }`; if the manifest is missing, build the list at load with `import.meta.glob('../../assets/music/*.{mp3,ogg,wav,m4a}', { eager: true, query: '?url' })`.
- On every new level, pick a random track from a **shuffle bag** (no repeats until the bag is exhausted, then reshuffle). Crossfade 1.2 s from the previous track. Loop the track.
- On Game Over, duck to 20 % volume; on main menu, pick one track and loop it.
- If no tracks are found: silent, one `console.warn`, HUD shows "music: none". Do not crash and do not synthesise placeholder music.
- Mute toggle `M`; music volume slider separate from SFX.

### 12.2 Sound effects

The ComfyUI server only produces images, so SFX are **synthesised at runtime with WebAudio** (no audio files needed, zero licensing risk, easy to tune). One shared implementation file `src/audio/sfx.js`, with an optional override: if `assets/audio/sfx/<name>.<ext>` exists, that file wins — so the user can drop real recordings in later without code changes.

Required bank: `swing_whoosh`, `hit_metal`, `hit_flesh`, `hit_slime`, `bow_draw`, `bow_release`, `arrow_impact`, `fireball_cast`, `fireball_impact`, `ghost_moan`, `ghost_hit`, `slime_squelch`, `orc_grunt`, `orc_death`, `archer_call`, `pickup_gear`, `equip_upgrade`, `salvage`, `heal`, `extra_life`, `armor_break`, `player_hurt`, `player_death`, `stairs_start`, `stairs_complete`, `menu_click`, `menu_back`, `level_start`, `boss_roar`, `distant_drip`, `distant_skitter`, `distant_stone`.

All SFX pitch-jitter ±8 % and voice-limit 6 simultaneous. Positional via `PannerNode` (HRTF) for enemy sounds, 2D for UI and player.

## 13. Asset generation with the `z_image_turbo` MCP workflow

### 13.1 Generation rules (hard constraints)

1. Call `get_workflow_template` for `z_image_turbo` and start every generation from that returned graph.
2. Patch **only** these six inputs:
   | Field | Node | Input |
   |---|---|---|
   | prompt | `57:27` | `text` |
   | width | `57:13` | `width` |
   | height | `57:13` | `height` |
   | seed | `57:3` | `seed` |
   | steps | `57:3` | `steps` |
   | output prefix | `9` | `filename_prefix` |
3. Never touch `57:28` (UNET `z_image_turbo_fp16.safetensors`), `57:30` (CLIP `qwen_3_4b.safetensors`, lumina2), `57:29` (VAE `ae.safetensors`), `57:11` (shift 3), CFG 1, `res_multistep`, `simple`, denoise 1, `ConditioningZeroOut`, or any connection.
4. Always submit with `generate_with_workflow`. Never use `generate_image` (it is checkpoint-based and would load a different model).
5. Never `save_workflow_template` with test values, and never `overwrite: true` on `z_image_turbo` unless the user explicitly asks.
6. Steps: **8** for everything. Sizes: 1024×1024 for textures, enemies, props, menu art; 512×512 for pickups, icons, decals.
7. Seed discipline: fixed documented seed per final asset; when exploring, generate 3–4 seeds and record which one was chosen.

### 13.2 Known capability limits of this graph (do not work around with other models)

- **Negated clauses inside the prompt make the thing appear.** This graph samples at CFG 1 with the negative branch wired to `ConditioningZeroOut`, so a `negative_prompt` is discarded entirely, and any `no X` phrase typed into the *positive* prompt is simply a description of X that the model then paints. Observed directly: "no dots" produced a lattice of dots, "no teal, no turquoise" produced teal, "no blue, no cyan" produced blue chips, and "no pictograms" is the likeliest cause of the pictograms on the first-pass `pillar`, `door_oak` and `cobweb`. **Write prompts affirmatively**: name the palette, name the arrangement ("evenly distributed all-over detail", "clean unbroken background"), and never name a thing you do not want. Do not pass a `negative_prompt` and assume it worked. The flip side of naming only what you want: **do not name the medium either.** Describing a coin as a "bold game pickup icon" embossed a modern games controller onto it. Describe the object as a thing in the world ("a worn gold piece, plain blank face"), and reserve framing language for composition and background.
- **No inpainting, no outpainting, no img2img inside this graph.** Regenerate with a new seed instead of editing. `refine_image` (img2img) exists as a separate MCP tool but runs a *different* workflow, so it is only for optional polish on already-approved assets, with `denoise ≤ 0.35`, and never as a substitute for a good prompt.
- **No upscaler models are installed on the server** (`upscale_models` is empty). `upscale_image` is therefore unavailable; do not depend on it. Get detail by prompting and, if needed, generating at 1024 and downscaling to the display size in-engine.
- **Some ordinary words are objects to this model, not descriptions.** Each of these cost a
  generation and was fixed by describing the *result* instead of the cause or the analogy:
  "crescent" painted a moon; "the swept path of a heavy sword swing" painted a literal gold
  sword with hilt and crossguard; "ribbons of mist breaking into wisps" painted a feather;
  "molten" and "burning" put flame tongues on a spark sprite; "globe with rolling folds"
  produced continent-shaped blotches (same failure as the coin's map blotches); "where the
  ring meets the ground" painted a smear on the floor. For an effect, describe what is
  visibly there — "a plain abstract curved band of light and dust with nothing solid inside
  it" — and never the thing that made it.
- **ControlNet and IP-Adapter availability is unverified** on this server. Style
  consistency comes from a shared prompt suffix and shared seeds, not from conditioning
  tools. If a future request needs pose/depth control, report the missing models rather
  than swapping generators.
- If a required MCP capability is missing, **report the exact tool or error** — do not substitute the default checkpoint model.

### 13.3 Shared prompt parts

**STYLE** (current, painted key — batch 3 onward) = `hand-painted stylized game asset, painterly PBR-adjacent rendering, soft cel-shaded key light from upper left, limited cohesive palette, bold readable shapes that stay legible at distance, slight visible brushwork, centered composition`

`_photoreal_v1` STYLE (batch 1-2, superseded; originals kept in `assets/images/_photoreal_v1/`) = `photorealistic AAA game asset, PBR material detail, crisp studio key light with cool rim light, subtle film grain, sharp focus, high dynamic range`

**BG-SPRITE** = `isolated on flat solid uniform magenta (#ff00ff) background, clean unbroken background, subject only, full body in frame`
The magenta line is load-bearing: the runtime keyer samples the image border and cuts on chroma. Phrase "subject contains no pink/magenta" by *naming the subject's palette affirmatively* instead of forbidding hues. Two measured consequences of that, both learned the hard way: **violet is not safe either** — it sits close enough to the keyed family that a violet ward-glow on armour would key out and leave holes in the cuirass, so glowing subjects are authored ochre/amber instead. And a pale near-white subject picks up magenta bounce off the field (the extra-life icon measured 0.67% subject tint against a 0.2% bar); the engine despills surviving pixels so it still passes, but author the pale things cool and away from the field where you can.

**BG-TILE** = `seamless tileable texture, flat top-down lighting, uniform scale, evenly distributed all-over detail, medium-frequency detail, soft brush-blended edges`
Say "evenly distributed" rather than "no large motifs", and "soft edges" rather than "no outlines" — see §13.2.

There is no NEG-WORDS suffix. It was removed: those clauses live in the positive prompt and were producing artefacts (see §13.2).

Prompt template for entities: `A <subject description>, full body, facing camera, <family/variant detail>, standing pose, ${STYLE}, <family palette named affirmatively>, ${BG-SPRITE}`

Prompt template for tiles: `${STYLE}, <material description>, <palette named affirmatively>, ${BG-TILE}`

### 13.4 Output handling

`generate_with_workflow` returns a URL like `http://10.0.0.99:8000/view?filename=<prefix>_00001_.png&subfolder=&type=output`. Download it, save under the canonical path with the canonical name (strip the `_00001_` counter), and append a record to `assets/images/manifest.json`:

```json
{ "path": "assets/images/enemies/t1/orc_grunt.png",
  "prompt": "...", "seed": 41021, "steps": 8, "size": [1024, 1024],
  "prefix": "strata-en-orc-grunt", "sourceUrl": "http://10.0.0.99:8000/view?...",
  "rejectedSeeds": [41017, 41018], "generatedAt": "2026-11-05T04:30:00Z" }
```

### 13.6 Selection pass

For any asset that fails review, regenerate with a different seed and record rejected seeds in the manifest. Review criteria: subject readable at 128 px, correct material, no text/watermark, background cleanly keyable, tile seams acceptable at 50 % offset. Budget up to 4 attempts per asset before reporting it as a generation problem.

**What the review actually measured.** Two QA harnesses do this mechanically, so the
pass is repeatable rather than eyeballed:

- `npm run qa:seams` → `seamcheck.png`: every tile at 50 % offset next to the engine's
  mirrored composite. Result: raw tiles all show seams, mirrored composites none (see
  §11) — so seam failure is *not* an asset defect and regeneration does not fix it.
- `npm run test:keys` → per-sprite numbers through the game's own keying pipeline
  (`keycheck.html` renders the table and thumbnails). Result: 57/57 clean.

The one asset that failed was `items/arrow`, twice. Studio-style prompts ("crisp studio
key light…") make the model paint a floor, a gradient and a cast shadow, and 10.4 % then
5.7 % of the image stayed magenta after keying. The prompt that works for thin props is
`viewed from directly above, product cutout sprite, background is a single flat solid
magenta colour rgb(255,0,255) filling every pixel edge to edge like a graphics-program
fill`. The keyer also gained an absolute-chroma rule (`src/render/chromaKey.js`) because
border sampling alone cannot see a gradient's far side; `keycheck.html` reports
"subject eaten" so that rule stays verifiable against purple subjects (void slime,
archmage: 0.4 % eaten, still clean).

---

### 13.7 Alpha conversion pass (second model, Qwen-Image-2.1)

Z-Image Turbo cannot emit alpha, which is why the whole art set sits on a magenta field and
is keyed at runtime. That costs quality exactly where softness matters — glow, smoke, wet
splatter — because the feathered band picks up the field colour. Qwen-Image-2.1 on the second
box can emit real RGBA, **if asked in a particular way**:

- The instruction begins *"the image contains an alpha channel."* and ends
  *"transparent background"*, with the graph's prompt enhancer switched off, because the
  enhancer paraphrases the framing away. Asked plainly, the model paints the field white and
  writes alpha 255 across the frame — an RGBA file with zero transparent pixels.
- Every result is measured, never eyeballed: fully-clear share ≥ 15%, opaque subject ≥ 10%,
  and silhouette overlap ≥ 0.35 against the already-approved art (measured 0.94–0.96 in
  practice, so the subject does hold). The semi-transparent band arrives violet regardless of
  the input background and is corrected offline, leaving opaque pixels untouched.
- **Excluded from this pass on purpose:** `textures/**` (walls, floors and ceilings tile and
  must be solid — transparency there would show through the level), the decal kinds, which
  already carry code-side alpha masks, and anything rendered as geometry. This pass is for
  billboards: enemies, items, effects.
- Promotion over a shipped image is a separate, explicit step: the previous file is copied to
  `assets/images/_chroma_v1/` and the manifest record gains the conversion's model, licence,
  seed and measurements while keeping the original generation's provenance.

### 13.8 Animated sprites from a video model (built; phase 1 in flight)

The second box holds Wan 2.2, LTX-2.3 and MiniMax H3 checkpoints. Licensing decides the
choice more than quality does: **Wan 2.2 is Apache 2.0** with no revenue or field-of-use
limits, **LTX-2** is a community licence that is free commercially below $10M annual revenue
and carries competitive-use and training clauses, and MiniMax terms are proprietary — so the
animation pass runs on Wan unless that changes.

**The graph.** The owner-supplied 14B i2v export lives in `workflows/wan22_i2v.json` with a
metadata header naming the patchable nodes. `tools/graphCheck.mjs` validates a graph against
a server's *own* `object_info` before anything is queued: every class exists, every input
name is real (including ComfyUI's flattened `values.a` / `format.codec` sub-widgets), every
model file named by a loader is in that loader's list, and every link points at a node that
is present. That check earns its keep — the same graph is structurally invalid on the art
box, whose `CreateVideo` predates four of its inputs, and the failure would otherwise have
surfaced as a dead queue slot.

**Shape of the work.** The approved still is the model's first frame, so the clip inherits
the sprite's identity rather than asking a video model to invent a creature. Wan returns a
video with no alpha, so the sprite is flattened onto a flat backdrop first, and every frame
comes back through a keyer. Backdrop choice is measured per sprite, not picked by taste:
`tools/videoKit.mjs` projects the sprite's own opaque pixels onto each candidate backdrop's
hue axis and takes the 95th percentile as a collision score. Green loses badly on the slimes
(0.52) and wins for the spiders (−0.01), which is exactly the case a hand-picked chroma
colour gets wrong. The runtime keyer's magenta-specific rule became the same maths about an
arbitrary hue axis, and `npm run test:video` proves the round trip on shipped art before any
GPU minute is spent (38 checks: compose → key → compare against the source silhouette).

**Settings, from measurement.** Frame counts are 4n+1 because Wan's video VAE compresses
time by 4 (walk 17, attack/hurt 13, flee 17 at 16 fps), and the graph's duration input is
set to `(frames − 1) / fps` so its own `floor(a*b+1)` expression yields exactly that. On the
one clip where both paths were rendered from the same start frame, the **4-step lightx2v
LoRA path at CFG 1 (15 s) was visually equivalent to the 20-step CFG 3.5 path (57 s)** —
which means the *wording* of the motion prompt, not the sampler, is what controls the result,
and a full phase costs minutes. The trade-off is real and measured: as motion rises from
0.94% to 1.36% of the frame per step, worst silhouette overlap against the still falls from
0.80 to 0.64. Motion is bought with identity, so both are gated.

**Gates.** `scoreClip` in `tools/videoKit.mjs` is the single judge, called by the runner and
re-runnable over existing clips by `tools/animMeasure.mjs` with no generation — so a gate
that turns out too loose can be tightened across a whole phase and the honest re-verdict
printed. Ten gates: frame count, backdrop keyed every frame, subject never vanishes,
neighbour-frame agreement, identity held, first frame faithful, camera stayed put, no
recolouring, **the subject actually moves**, and **subject kept its facing**. The last two
were added after failure, and their floors come from data: a clip that is really a still
photograph scores 0% movement, so the floor is 0.6%; the first clips did not fail by going
still, they failed by quietly *rotating the creature sideways* while the centroid stayed
put — the rotating clip's silhouette box bottoms out at 0.82 of the first frame while the
clips that stepped in place stay above 0.87, hence a 0.85 floor, exempt for `flee` whose job
is to shrink. It is a proxy — a rotation that happened to preserve its box would pass —
which is why every clip still gets a contact sheet, and why nothing promotes itself.

Promotion is a separate deliberate step, as with the alpha pass: clips land in
`experiments/anim/<sprite>__<action>/` with `start.png`, the raw clip, per-frame keyed PNGs,
`sheet.png` and measured `results.json`, indexed by `list.json` for `animreview.html`.

**Shipping format: one animated WebP per clip, boomeranged, frames named at runtime.** The
animation is baked forward-then-reverse (1…*N*…*N*−1…2, endpoints not duplicated) so the loop
has no seam, and the file loops forever. But the file containing the animation is not what
plays it: measured in the browser the game runs in, an `<img>` of an animated WebP hands the
canvas **one frozen frame** no matter how long you wait, and this game must name a frame —
two creatures of the same kind never stand at the same moment, the player can pause, and an
idle monster should show its still sprite. The frames are therefore pulled out by index with
WebCodecs `ImageDecoder` (`src/render/animation.js`), decoded once per clip and shared. If
`ImageDecoder` is missing, the feature switches off and every billboard keeps today's static
sprite: animation is a garnish, never a dependency.

Two browser details cost time and are recorded so nobody relearns them: `ImageDecoder` needs
an **ArrayBuffer**, and a Blob throws a type error that looks like the API is absent; and this
build reports `selectedTrack === null` and `complete === true` on the *first* frame, so frame
count comes from the container the build tool verified, not from decoder metadata. The build
tool verifies the container by walking RIFF chunks (`tools/webpParse.mjs`) because ffmpeg
here cannot re-read the animated WebP it writes and `webpmux` is not installed: animation
flag, loop count, frame count, canvas size and a per-frame alpha plane are all asserted before
a file is kept. GIF is ruled out on quality grounds rather than support — its transparency is
one bit per pixel, and every sprite here has soft feathered edges.

Measured cost, full enemy roster: **49 clips, 4.6 MB**, site payload 38.0 → 42.2 MB. That is
walk and attack for every species (23 distinct drawings across four tiers — the spider
family's tier-4 slot reuses the tier-3 art) plus flee for the three spiders, because
retreating is currently spider-only AI and an animation with no trigger is dead weight in the
download. Each clip is 10 unique frames boomeranged to 18 at 152 px, quality 70. A static
WebP of one frame is 7.5 KB against 51.8 KB as PNG with byte-identical alpha measurements, so
the format is worth roughly 7× at any frame count. **The 8-bit indexed fallback was measured
and rejected**: palette WebP came out 3× larger lossless and no smaller lossy than plain RGBA,
because ffmpeg re-expands it internally — cell size and frame count are the levers that work.
Full-resolution settings are on disk for anyone who wants them: the same roster at 192 px with
all frames projects near 18 MB.

### 13.9 Grittier environment surfaces and bump mapping (measured)

All 16 environment tiles were restyled through Qwen-Image-2.1 in **edit mode**, which
conditions on the existing tile, so the masonry layouts survive and only the surface changes.
Per-tile instructions and the seeds used live in `workflows/grit_prompts.json`; the pass is
re-runnable and arguable because the wording sits next to the other reviewed graphs.

Shipping got cheaper rather than dearer. The renderer caps a tile at 512 px inside the
mirrored composite, so the 1024 px PNGs were 15.5 MB of transfer for detail the browser
discarded. At the size actually used and encoded opaque WebP the tiles are 0.98 MB; normal
maps add 1.01 MB and roughness maps 0.3 MB. The site is 29.1 MB, down from 42.2 MB.

**Normal maps are derived offline, not generated.** Luminance → wrapping box blur → Sobel →
normalise (`tools/normalFromAlbedo.mjs`). A normal map is geometry rather than imagery, so
deriving it from the tile's own shading guarantees the relief agrees with the albedo, it is
reproducible from source in milliseconds instead of GPU minutes, and no third-party terms
attach to it — the only generated thing in the chain is the surface.

**The trap the engine already contained.** The anti-seam mechanism is a mirrored 2×2
composite. For colour that is free; for a normal map it is wrong, because the stored colour
*is* a direction, so a mirrored quadrant must negate red across the vertical seam and green
across the horizontal. The self-test samples the seam at a strongly sloped texel and asserts
the normals stay continuous. Roughness maps store no direction, so their composite is a plain
geometric flip — recorded in the code so nobody "fixes" it later.

**What bump mapping is actually worth here, measured rather than assumed.** The headlamp is a
spotlight rigidly attached to the camera, so a wall facing the player is lit along its own
normal; a tilted micro-normal barely changes N·L, and a normal map cannot invent the
self-shadowing that makes a deep joint read as a hole. With the game's real light values and
the shipped crypt wall (`bumpcheck.html`, `npm run qa:bump`):

| surface | normalScale 1.4 — pixels changed by bump | surface change across a 0.55 m sidestep |
|---|---|---|
| matte 0.88, no sheen map, head-on | 0.60% | 5.86% → 5.89% |
| engine wall 0.88 + sheen map, head-on | 1.07% | 5.96% → 6.11% |
| worn 0.62 + sheen map, head-on | 2.07% | 5.53% → 6.68% |
| matte 0.88, no sheen, beside a torch | 1.77% | 9.01% → 9.26% |
| worn 0.62 + sheen, beside a torch | 2.68% | 8.99% → 10.24% |

Read honestly: the normal map alone changes well under 1% of pixels and is invisible on
screen — the owner reported exactly that, and the measurement agrees. The roughness companion
is what adds anything a player can notice, and it works because it is view-dependent: the
sheen slides across the worn faces while the player moves, which is where the eye reads
relief. Getting relief that survives a still frame needs actual occlusion — screen-space
ambient occlusion, shadow-casting torches, or displaced geometry — and the level deliberately
runs faked lighting with shadow maps off (§16), so that is a separate, measurable decision
rather than a default.

### 13.10 Prop and interface pass (one screenshot from the owner plus five requests)

- **Cobwebs mount to the room.** They were groups of planes with a random snapped yaw, so in a
  cell open on all four sides a web floated in mid-air. `wallFaces` returns up to two
  perpendicular solid faces; `wallMount` walks outward two cells when the prop cell has none
  and hangs from the nearest wall, and a cobweb with no wall anywhere near is skipped rather
  than floated. The builder then places a sheet against each face, a web bridging them along
  the ceiling, and a drape into the corner. The self-test checks this geometrically — the sum
  of each group's child offsets must point at a solid neighbour — because a screenshot only
  proves a web looked mounted by luck of the camera.
- **Floor decals carry their own silhouette.** Blood and scorch tiles were opaque squares of
  floor, and the square edge was hidden with a radial alpha mask, which is why they read as
  pools of light. They went back through the image model for isolation on a flat chroma
  backdrop and were keyed here (`tools/decalAlpha.mjs`: 87.4% and 80.9% of the frame keyed to
  clear, shipped at 11 KB and 17 KB). `textureHasAlpha` probes the art, and the radial mask is
  now applied only to decals that still need it.
- **Minimap follows the player.** `mapWindow` is a pure function, exported so it can be
  asserted, returning the cell window, its offset and the pixels per cell; levels smaller than
  `CFG.mapViewCells` still draw whole, larger ones scroll, north stays up, and only the
  visible cell range is drawn.
- **Fullscreen is the element API, not F11.** `V`, or the pause-menu button, calls
  `document.documentElement.requestFullscreen` and resizes the renderer on
  `fullscreenchange` and again on the next frame, so the picture is rendered at the panel's
  pixel count instead of the same image stretched over a bigger window. F11 is intercepted and
  routed to the same path, and a browser that refuses the request says why rather than doing
  nothing.
- **Props got surfaces.** A bone tile (`textures/bone`, with derived normal and roughness maps)
  went onto the bone piles; rubble and debris already carry the biome masonry. The chain's end
  piece — a bare iron rod, which read as a modelling mistake — is now a low-poly skull with
  dark sockets, shared with the bone piles.

Harness note: the screenshot tool runs Edge with `--disable-gpu`, and SwiftShader cannot
rasterise the displaced walls at all, so prop and decal screenshots are taken with `?disp=0`.
That is a limitation of the harness, not of the game.

### 13.11 Generated sound effects (Stable Audio 3)

§12.2 assumed the ComfyUI boxes produced images only, so the 35 sound events were synthesised
at runtime from WebAudio recipes — a good call at the time, and the fallback is still there.
Stable Audio 3 changed that: `src/audio/sfx.js` already preferred a file in
`assets/audio/sfx/<name>` over its recipe, so replacing the bank was a naming job rather than
a code change.

- **Graph**: `workflows/stable_audio_sfx.json`, the owner's MCP graph with the LLM reprompt
  chain removed (an enhancer at temperature 0.7 rewrites each description differently on every
  run — the same reason the prompt enhancer is off on the image boxes). Node ids are preserved.
  Validated against the server's own inventory by `tools/graphCheck.mjs`.
- **Descriptions**: `workflows/sfx_prompts.json`, one per event in the model's own SFX style
  (source, material, space, temporal evolution, then `Length: N seconds`, which must agree
  with the graph's duration input or the clip truncates mid-decay).
- **Batch**: `tools/sfxBatch.mjs` (npm run `sfx:batch`), strictly one generation in flight.
  It measures each clip from decoded PCM samples — this ffmpeg build has no working stats
  filters, verified — and gates on: length against the request, peak between −26 and −0.6
  dBFS, audible body against the category, dead air before the attack, a hard cut at the end,
  and a 240 KB size ceiling. Accepted clips are level-matched to a −6 dBFS peak (gain capped
  at +9 dB so a quiet clip is not lifted into its own noise floor) before shipping.
- **What the gates caught** that a listening pass would catch late: a bow draw with 0.26 s of
  dead air before the sound starts; impacts so short they were only 0.1 s of body. Two earlier
  bugs in the harness itself are recorded in its comments — history outputs are keyed by node
  id (`outputs["57"].audio`), which made successful runs look like failures, and counting a
  fading room tail as silence rejected every honest one-shot, because a sword whoosh *is*
  0.16 s of sound plus a second of room.
- **Objective signal that the descriptions land**: zero-crossing rate separates them cleanly —
  a water drip at 6046/s, a metallic clang at 6537, a sword whoosh at 3189, a flesh hit at
  3279, a spectral moan at 1984 — and the boss roar carries by far the highest mean level.
  Timbre and loudness are the thing the owner judges by ear; defects are what is measured here.
- **Licence**: the model is tagged `license:other` / `stable-audio-community` on Hugging Face,
  with the licence link pointing at Stability AI's community licence, and the upstream
  `stabilityai` repositories are gated behind accepting terms. The full text was not readable
  in this session without an authenticated account; the owner was told this on 2026-11-07 and
  instructed to generate and ship the bank. That instruction is the approval on record — this
  document is not licence advice.
- **Guard**: the self-test asserts every event name has a generated file and that no shipped
  clip is unreferenced, because a missing clip falls back to the synthesised placeholder and
  would otherwise survive the whole suite sounding merely thin.

### 13.13 The soundtrack, first attempt (MiniMax-Music3)

**Outcome first: the owner listened to all six cues and rejected every one**, then supplied
tracks from their own backlog instead — see §13.13.1. Nothing from this pass ships, so the
UI-naming obligation described below was removed again with it. The pass is still recorded
because the graph, the gates and the discovery about cue length are reusable and were not
wasted.

Six cues: one per biome plus a boss cue and a title theme. The owner
planned to compose these themselves and had better luck with MiniMax and Ace Step than with
Stable Audio for music, so their MCP graph became `workflows/minimax_music3.json` with node
ids preserved — the only change being the default caption and lyrics, since their example is a
lo-fi hip-hop song with verses.

**Licence, read rather than inferred.** The Music3 weights carry a *MiniMax-Music3 Community
License* and the full text is readable in the public `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-Music3` repository,
unlike Stability's, which sits behind a gated repo. It permits distribution and commercial
use, subject to naming the model in the product UI, disclosing machine-generated content, and
separate written authorisation above $20M aggregate yearly revenue; the heavier obligations in
§4 apply only to products that let third parties generate with the model, which this is not.
Both applicable obligations are implemented: `AUDIO_CREDIT_HTML` in `src/ui/menus.js` names
MiniMax-Music3 on the main menu and in How to Play, and `assets/music/credits.json` ships
inside the build with the attribution chain (fine-tuned from Qwen3-8B Apache-2.0, DiT from
stable-audio-tools MIT, VAE from Descript Audio Codec MIT). `tools/checkBuild.mjs` fails the
build if that credit is absent from `dist/`.

**Length is structural, not a parameter.** The first pass produced cues of 17–35 s against a
60–75 s request; one cue happened to hit exactly 75 s. Adding "this loops, do not fade out" to
the caption did nothing (13–28 s on the re-roll). The real lever is the `lyrics` field:
`MiniMaxMusic3TextEncode` returns a duration of its own choosing and
`EmptyMiniMaxMusic3LatentAudio` is built from that value, so `max_duration` is only a ceiling
the model is free to come in under. The owner's working example carried ten named section
markers; the briefs carried only `[Instrumental]`. With eight markers the same cue came back
at 53.7 s. The asks were then set to what that structure delivers (60 s per biome, 50 s boss)
rather than loosening the length gate — a 54 s seamless loop is a perfectly good biome bed,
and asking for 75 s while the gate punishes 54 s is just a way of manufacturing rejects.

**Cues loop, so the briefs stop asking for endings.** `music.js` sets `loop = true`, and the
first briefs asked for layers dropping away into silence; a fade-out is an ending, and every
cycle would have restarted from a gap. The shared playback instruction now asks for an ending
that matches the opening in tempo, key and texture.

**Gates** (`tools/musicBatch.mjs`, measuring through the shared `tools/audioMeter.mjs`): length
against the ask, silence before the first note, a hard cut instead of decay at the end, and
**loudness in four quarters with a 12 dB ceiling on the spread** — the check that matters for
music, because a cue that dies in its middle or swells into a wall at the end is invisible to
a single average and immediately obvious under a crossfade. The clipping threshold is far
looser than the SFX one (120 flat samples in a row rather than 8): this model masters hot,
brief overs that touch full scale are inaudible and the level-match pulls them down, while a
sustained run is real distortion. Shipped copies are level-matched to a −20 dBFS mean and
re-encoded at a lower bitrate than the master (~1 MB per 75 s cue) because the soundtrack is
the largest single asset group in the site.

**Selection is by filename prefix**, so `caverns.mp3` answers to The Caverns and a boss depth
prefers the boss cue, with a shuffle bag over everything as the fallback — a soundtrack
covering three biomes still plays something everywhere. The self-test asserts every biome in
`biomes.order` has a cue, that a boss and title cue exist, and that the licence credit names
the model.

### 13.13.1 The soundtrack that shipped: the owner's own ACE-Step 1.5 cues

Eight ambient tracks from the owner's backlog, dropped into `assets/music/` at 78 MB — more
than double the rest of the site. `tools/musicPack.mjs` re-encodes to 128 kbps MP3 (the owner
asked for 128k MP3 or Ogg; MP3 won because Safari cannot play Ogg Vorbis and the game plays
music through `new Audio(url)`), level-matches every cue to a −20 dBFS mean, and writes to
`experiments/` for review before anything lands in the game. **78 MB became 30.3 MB**, and the
originals moved to `music_sources/`, which git ignores, so the masters survive.

One cue had 23.9 s of near-silence before the first note — lovely on an album, a bug when it is
the first thing a fresh depth plays — so `--map "name = cavern@auto"` trims the measured
lead-in with a short fade. Every cue now sits between −19.9 and −20.5 dBFS mean, gains of
−2.6 to −5.3 dB, so descending never changes the volume.

**Biome assignment was measured, and the measurement had a bug.** The first profiler labelled
four low-pass filters as four bands, so it reported a darkness of 0.47–0.49 for every track —
a low-pass at 4 kHz is nearly the whole signal, so those were cumulative energies, not bands.
Had I trusted it, the soundtrack would have been named by a meter that could not tell a bass
drone from a bright lead. Bands are now differences of cumulative low-pass energy, and
`tools/audioProfileSelftest.mjs` checks them against pure tones (60/90/300/900/1500/5000 Hz
each landing in the right band, darkness 0.98 at 80 Hz against 0.007 at 5 kHz) — 7 passed,
with the onset self-test skipped because this ffmpeg build has no `atremolo` filter.

What the corrected profiler says, and how each cue was placed:

| source | darkness | onsets/s | placed as | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ACE…00018 | 0.864 | 0.50 | crypt | lowest and stillest: oppressive and patient |
| ACE…00002 | 0.822 | 1.85 | cavern | mid-dark with movement, 23 s of silence trimmed |
| Funky Upbeat | 0.877 | 2.40 | foundry | the most rhythmic of the mid-energy pieces |
| ACE…00025 | 0.819 | 0.92 | vault | broadest spectrum, slow, densest level |
| soundblaster_00002 | 0.782 | 2.82 | boss | brightest and most driven of the set |
| really_nice | 0.848 | 2.14 | title | moderate energy, welcoming enough for a menu |
| soundblaster_00001 | 0.812 | 0.38 | vault_02 | the stillest cue, paired with the vault |
| Nice mello tune | 0.801 | 3.02 | cavern_02 | brighter, busiest — variety for the caverns |

That table is honest about its limits: darkness, brightness and onset rate correlate with mood,
but they are not mood. The owner has heard these tracks and I have not, so the mapping is
offered as a first draft — swapping any two is one `musicPack` invocation.

**Licence**: ACE-Step's repository is MIT, while the Ace-Step 1.5 weights repo had an open
request for a LICENSE file, and hosted ACEMusic.ai output may carry separate service terms.
These are the owner's own tracks from their backlog, so the rights position is theirs; the
question is recorded in `assets/music/credits.json` rather than assumed away. The credit line
in the UI now names ACE-Step 1.5 for music and Stable Audio 3 for effects, and still states
that the audio is machine-generated.

## 14. Project structure

```
DungeonGame/
  index.html styles.css vite.config.js
  README.md GAME_DESIGN_SPEC.md image_z_image_turbo_api.json
  seamcheck.html            tile seam review sheet (§13.6)
  keycheck.html             per-sprite chroma-key QA (§13.6)
  src/
    boot.js                 URL params, boot, self-test hook
    main.js                 scene, loop, state machine, run/level/descend, pickups
    config.js               tuning constants (§16)
    input.js                pointer lock, WASD, interact, pause, mute
    selftest.js             20 in-browser integration checks
    world/
      levelGen.js           §9 generator + validator (backtracker, braid, rooms)
      levelView.js          instanced walls, floor/ceiling, props, torches, staircase
      collision.js          circle-vs-grid slide, LOS, findOpenSpot
      spawner.js            enemy/loot placement, drop rolls, tier tables
    entity/
      player.js             movement, damage resolution, viewmodel
      enemy.js              shared FSM + the six family behaviours (§6)
      pickup.js             float, magnet, contact → equip/salvage/consume
      effects.js            projectiles, VFX, damage numbers
    loot/quality.js         §8 tier weights, jitter, endless scaling
    render/
      assets.js             glob registry, placeholders, mirrored tiles, sprite downscale
      chromaKey.js          backdrop-sampled keying + absolute-chroma rule + despill
    ui/hud.js minimap.js toasts.js menus.js
    audio/music.js (§12.1) sfx.js (§12.2)
    util/rng.js grid.js storage.js
  tools/
    validateLevels.mjs simulateLoot.mjs testMovement.mjs   headless Node suites
    runSelfTest.mjs keyCheck.mjs pageShot.mjs              headless-browser harnesses
  data/
    enemies.json items.json quality.json biomes.json levels.json
  assets/
    images/                 generated (§13) + manifest.json (88 records)
      textures/ enemies/<t1..t4>/ props/ items/ vfx/ ui/
    music/                  USER-SUPPLIED, ships empty + manifest.json
    audio/sfx/              optional overrides, ships empty
```

The original sketch listed `combat/`, `state/`, `enemyAI/`, `render/sprites.js` and
`lights.js` as separate modules; the build folded them into `entity/`, `main.js` and
`levelView.js` because the seams were imaginary at this size — the behaviour they were
meant to isolate lives in `entity/enemy.js` (family behaviours), `entity/player.js` and
`entity/effects.js` (damage application), and the light pool in `world/levelView.js`.

`util/rng.js` must implement a seeded PRNG (mulberry32 or sfc32). Never use `Math.random()` for level, spawn, drop, or quality rolls — otherwise seed reproducibility and this document's testing claims are void. `Math.random()` is allowed only for cosmetic jitter.

## 15. Data-driven tables

No stat may be hard-coded in gameplay code. `data/enemies.json`, `data/items.json`, `data/quality.json`, `data/biomes.json` hold everything in §6 and §8; engine code reads them. Every number in §6, §8, and §16 is a **starting value** expected to change under the §19 tuning harness.

## 17. Gap-fill decisions

These were not in the request. They are my calls; flag any you want reversed.

1. **First-person, 2.5D sprite entities** rather than 3D meshes — the asset generator makes images, and photoreal sprites in a real lit maze is the honest way to get the requested look.
2. **Damage model:** armour = mitigation tier + durability that soaks 65 % of hits; armour partially repairs on descent. Makes the armour bar matter moment-to-moment.
3. **Lives = 3, cap 5;** death costs a life and respawns you at the level entry, not to Game Over. Game Over only when lives reach 0, per the request.
4. **Arrow ammunition (reversed after play).** Infinite ammo was tried and the bow outclassed the sword with no cost. Arrows are now a counted resource: 1–3 per archer killed, one spent per shot, and an empty quiver locks the ranged slot.
5. **Salvage instead of discard** for weaker items — gives a score sink and makes junk drops feel useful.
6. **Quality tiers with colour-coded glow** rather than 6 separate art variants per item — 78 assets instead of ~400, and rarity stays readable.
7. **Miniboss every 3rd depth** with a guaranteed high-tier drop. Without a spike, depth 3/6/9 are just more of the same.
8. **Ghost armour-piercing damage** and one-wall-per-4-s phase limit. Armour-pierce makes ghosts a real threat that punishes over-reliance on the armour bar; the phase limit keeps them fair.
9. **Slime split on death (30 %)** — makes the most common drop source slightly dangerous.
10. **Minimap + stair sense at depth 5+** — pure maze search gets tedious past depth 5; this preserves the maze without the chore.
11. **Biomes every 3 depths** with their own tileset and palette, aligned with enemy tiers, so visual and difficulty progression happen on the same beat.
12. **Seeded runs** with a seed field in the menu, and a best-5 run table in `localStorage`.
13. **SFX synthesised in WebAudio**, with an optional `assets/audio/sfx/` override folder, since the MCP server can only generate images.
14. **`compareMode` settings toggle** (default off) so auto-equip never feels like theft to players who care about weapon families.
15. **Spider family is optional flavour** — drop it if the asset count needs trimming.

## 18. Build order / milestones

| # | Milestone | Contents | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|
| M0 | Boot + maze render | seeded generator, instanced walls/floor, placeholder grey boxes, WASD + pointer lock | you can walk a validated 25×25 maze |
| M1 | Validation + stairs | §9.1 validator, staircase placement + hold-to-descend, depth banner, level regeneration | 200 generated levels pass validation in a headless test |
| M2 | Combat | player melee, one enemy family (orc) with tell/attack, damage numbers, hurt feedback, health bar | you can kill and be killed by orcs |
| M3 | Loot + auto-upgrade | drops, quality rolls, contact auto-equip, armour bar, salvaging, toasts | touching gear visibly changes stats |
| M4 | Full enemy roster | all 6 families + AI + projectiles + miniboss | all behaviours present at Tier 1 |
| M5 | Asset pipeline | run all §13 generations, chroma-key loader, sprites, textures, viewmodel, UI frames | grey boxes replaced by generated art everywhere |
| M6 | Audio + polish | music shuffle-bag system, full SFX bank, fog/lights, minimap, menus, game over | a stranger can play a full run unaided |
| M7 | Tuning pass | §19 harness, 10 playthroughs, constant adjustments | median death depth lands in 6–12 |

M5 is deliberately late: grey-box first, because generation and keying are cheap once the slots exist.

**Stretch goals:** 3D meshes for enemies (projected texture onto low-poly forms), gamepad support, seed sharing via URL, controller remap, a "photoreal mode" toggle for higher post-FX.

## 19. Testing & tuning harness

- `?seed=1234&depth=7` URL params jump straight to a state — required for tuning.
- **In-run cheat for manual testing:** while paused, `L` then one or two digits jumps the run to that depth (`L 0 5` → 5, `L 1 0` → 10). It runs through the ordinary level-load path, so a cheated depth is a genuine generated level with genuine spawns. It is a remembered chord rather than a menu option so it cannot fire during play, and the pause card carries one quiet line reminding you it exists.
- Headless generation test: 200 levels per difficulty band, assert §9.1 on each, print path-length histogram. Target: median shortest path ≥ 0.55 × diameter, zero unreachable entities.
- Drop simulation (no rendering): simulate 10 000 kill-drops per depth band, assert mean item score rises with depth and stddev of same-depth drops ≥ 15 % (the "not always the same" requirement, made measurable).
- **Hosting check:** `npm run build && npm run check:build` serves the built `dist/` from a plain static file server — not the dev server — and runs the integration suite against it with every image loaded. It also rejects absolute asset paths and reports the payload size. The game is static-only and is published from GitHub Actions; nothing in the design requires a runtime server.
- Balance bot: a scripted player with fixed reaction time; report depth-at-death distribution over 100 runs. Accept target 6–12.
- Manual checklist: 10 playthroughs, log per-depth time, and note any depth where progression stalls or spikes.

---

## 20. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Chroma key leaves magenta fringe on photoreal sprites | 1 px feather + despill in `chromaKey.js`; fallback backdrop is flat mid-grey with luma key; never a white backdrop (kills dark sprites) |
| "Seamless tileable" prompts produce visible seams | 50 %-offset review step, regenerate with new seed, never patch in-engine |
| Photoreal sprites look pasted-on | contact-shadow decal, fog falloff matching sprite lighting, shared light direction baked into prompts (`key light from upper left`) |
| CFG 1 + zeroed negative means bad prompt words cannot be excluded | every prompt ends in explicit `no text, no watermark` phrasing; extra attempts with new seeds |
| Too many dynamic lights | 6-light pool by distance, emissive torches, no per-tile shadows |
| Ghost through-wall attacks feel unfair | one wall per 4 s, moan audio cue 0.8 s before contact, sprite always audible |
| Auto-equip takes a weapon the player preferred | `compareMode` toggle, always-visible delta toast |
| Empty `assets/music/` breaks a build | glob + manifest both optional, silent fallback with one warning |
| No upscaler models on the server | generate at final size (1024/512), downscale in-engine; do not call `upscale_image` |
| Scope creep on art | 78-asset cap in §13.5 is the budget; anything beyond it needs a decision, not a silent addition |

---

## 21. Acceptance criteria

1. A run plays start to finish: main menu → depth 1 → descend repeatedly → Game Over at 0 lives → results screen → retry.
2. Every level passes the solvability contract; the staircase is always reachable; no run can soft-lock.
3. Both HUD bars are always visible, with the empty-armor state shown as a disabled bar.
4. Auto-upgrade fires on contact with better gear, and the salvage path fires for worse gear; two identical drops on one level differ in score (quality jitter).
5. Each enemy family drops the correct item type; harder reskins drop the same types at higher quality tiers.
6. Lives decrement on death, Game Over only at zero.
7. A random music track starts on every new level from `assets/music/`, with no repeat before the bag empties, and the game runs silently-but-correctly when that folder is empty.
8. Every visible pixel in the game other than DOM text and canvas-drawn minimap lines originates from a `z_image_turbo` generation recorded in `assets/images/manifest.json`.
9. `z_image_turbo` template in the MCP registry is unmodified (same node graph, same models, same CFG/sampler/scheduler/shift) and no generation ever used the default checkpoint-based generator.
10. A run is reproducible from its seed alone.
